    Hosted portability follow-up — 3 November 2026

    Source: MAINTENANCE.md

    Published baseline: 0046842. The earlier audit below is historical; its publication-status statements predate that main commit.

    The Windows job reported four integrity failures because base R’s Sys.readlink() returns empty strings on Windows. Link detection now uses the explicit fs dependency, so native file/directory links, dangling links and junctions cannot be accepted as canonical members or overwrite destinations. Overwrite preflight also refuses a linked cellspec.json before parsing it.

    The new synthetic regressions fail seven assertions against the frozen baseline. The complete local suite passed 1,223 assertions with no failures or warnings; the native Windows junction case is intentionally reserved for Windows. Local coverage is 95.92644%, above the configured 90% floor. Shared house lint and workflow validation pass. Full source-package check passed with zero errors, zero warnings and one incoming-submission/development-version NOTE. Independent source review checked the fs/libuv Windows link classification and the no-read sidecar guard. Package-check results and exact-head hosted outcomes are retained with the follow-up evidence.

    The oldrel-3 row’s unavailable optional anndataR dependency is a separate informational compatibility observation. No R minimum, dependency requirement, test, or hosted gate was weakened. Checksums still detect consistency rather than producer identity; filesystem races are not an OS sandbox or lock.

    Contracts: R readlink behavior and fs file-type queries.

    Maintenance audit — 30 October 2026

    Public baseline: bd940f1baf937cd6a78f8741193ac419d34c712b (1.1.0). The local main checkout is 49 commits behind and remains untouched. This isolated branch starts from current public main. No patient data, fixtures or existing source exports are changed. GitHub has no open issues; baseline hosted checks pass, but do not establish the candidate’s readiness.

    Purpose and acceptance criteria

    cellspecR carries segmented microscopy measurements between tools with explicit units, identifiers, signal policies and provenance. A dependable release must preserve identifiers and representable values, reject partial or ambiguous imports, protect existing destinations on failure, and distinguish verified self-contained storage from data that depend on external paths. The local app must review the selected source and expose only results of a successful read. Public function signatures and the cellspec 1.0 contract remain stable.

    Findings and roadmap

    Priority Confirmed evidence and impact Changes and validation
    Essential cs_write_npy(list(1), existing) truncates an existing file to zero bytes before rejecting the input. Encode before opening the destination. Preserve previous bytes on invalid input; test successful NumPy interchange.
    Essential A destination created during cs_write() is replaced even with overwrite=FALSE; a file added during overwrite can also be deleted. .cs_commit_stage() never reads its overwrite argument or repeats the replaceability check. Recheck the destination at commit time and retain staging cleanup/rollback. Exercise a concurrent appearance and late unrelated file. This does not provide cross-process locking.
    Essential cs_verify() ignores .extra and accepts a data symlink pointing outside the directory. Include hidden entries and refuse symlink members without following directory links; reject unsafe portable paths, and verify control files too. Test relocation, modification, missing files and external links.
    Essential Actual NumPy 2.0.2 fixtures: int32 minimum becomes NA; uint32 at 2^31 and signed int64 values error on R’s reserved integer NA bit pattern. Exact 2^53 is rejected. Duplicate archive names silently resolve twice to the first member. Decode unsigned halves without R’s signed-integer sentinel; preserve supported exact range through +/-2^53; reject ambiguous archives. Compare both byte orders with independently generated NumPy fixtures and NumPy reads of R output.
    Essential A QuPath table with two valid rows and a broken footer imports silently as two cells. IDs 001/002 become 1/2. Treat parser warnings as format errors and preserve zero-prefixed/large integer identifiers. Exercise valid and truncated exports and provenance counts.
    Everyday use The app reads the upload temporary path rather than the supplied filename; RDS/gzip dispatch and derived image identity depend on suffix/basename. Failed reads retain previous data and downloads. Stage uploads under a safe original basename in session-local storage; clear results when input changes and before read. Test RDS/gzip names, failure and real browser downloads.
    Documentation AnnData documentation claims a Python runtime is mandatory although anndataR supports native in-memory objects. Exercise the declared optional integrations and align their prerequisites with observed behavior.

    Milestone 1 repairs storage and numeric fidelity; milestone 2 qualifies imports and the application; milestone 3 runs clean installation, package checks, blocking lint, coverage, docs, interoperability and direct first use. A repair is complete only after its failure path and successful workflow both pass. External tool-produced microscopy fixtures, hosted OS/R candidate CI and CRAN submission remain release gates. New adapters, new scientific models, broad rewrites and large-array streaming are deferred.

    Authoritative references: NumPy format, AnnData implementations.

    Further confirmed integrity findings were repaired during review: sidecar channel_index=1.5 silently became 1, and distinct cell/image tuples containing carriage returns collided. Strict scalar/type checks now reject lossy metadata, and internal length-prefixed keys keep valid identifiers distinct. An adversarial malformed footer containing braces also made cli evaluate the external diagnostic as an expression. All external error-message forwarding in read/write/interop paths now inserts literal text, with a regression that must retain both the structured error class and the unevaluated expression. The original write probe used a removed test hook and did not create its intended race; commit-stage-baseline.log reproduces the actual defect directly against the baseline function. Regression tests inject the late write through the current completion function and check preserved source bytes.

    Verification

    Detailed baseline/probe and qualification logs are retained outside the package in ../../evidence/cellspecR/.

    • Baseline: 187 tests, 1,141 passing assertions, no failures/errors/warnings and five optional-integration skips. The first test command could not start because devtools is absent; testthat ran the baseline successfully.
    • Installed Bioconductor integrations now run: SpatialExperiment reproduces the original cells and measurements, and AnnData constructs an 80 by 4 native R InMemoryAnnData. Its test no longer treats any conversion error as success.
    • Independent NumPy 2.0.2 fixtures cover eight signed/unsigned, little/big-endian boundary arrays. NumPy also reads all four R-written array types with exact values, dimensions, Unicode strings and booleans. No Python dependency was added to the package.
    • A 100,000-cell, nine-feature synthetic round trip preserves exact cells and measurements in both formats. Observed write/read elapsed times are 0.591/0.404 seconds for Parquet and 2.389/3.572 seconds for compressed TSV on this machine; these are single-run measurements, not a platform-wide performance claim.
    • Both canonical formats round-trip cells and measurements exactly from a fresh installed package. Output protection, hidden files, symbolic links, malformed tables, preserved IDs and metadata types have direct regression tests.
    • The first complete source-package --as-cran check passes with zero errors, zero warnings and one NOTE (new submission/development version). The final frozen archive also passes with zero errors/warnings and the same single NOTE. All 1,210 installed test assertions pass, with zero failures, warnings or skips; examples, vignette rebuilds and both manuals pass. Two print snapshots were reviewed: their only differences are the intentional package version change; public API signature fixtures remain unchanged.
    • Measured test coverage is 95.91%, above the required 90% floor. Final frozen-source coverage confirms that result. Blocking CTTIR house lint has zero findings. Actionlint and git diff --check pass; shellcheck/pyflakes are unavailable for actionlint.
    • Installed Chromium journey reads an RDS upload through its original filename, preserves IDs 001/002 and sample-A, observes the correct coordinate conversion (rounded to two decimals in the table), and downloads validation/dictionary CSVs. A malformed next upload clears the previous review and exports not_run. No JavaScript errors. Both owned application servers were stopped. Desktop and 390 px screenshots were inspected; wide mobile tables now scroll horizontally by keyboard inside a focusable labelled region, without overflowing the page.
    • Documentation builds 66 HTML pages with 1,889 local references and no missing files. Pandoc emits deprecated math-option diagnostics; the build succeeds. README preview badge fetching is unavailable in this Pandoc build; the generated Markdown retains its existing remote badge links.
    • No high-confidence private-key/access-token patterns were found in the tracked text scan. This is a pattern scan, not a full-history security audit.

    First use

    Prerequisites: R >= 4.1 and the DESCRIPTION imports (including data.table >= 1.17.0). Shiny and optionally bslib/ggplot2 enable the local review application. SpatialExperiment, SingleCellExperiment, S4Vectors and anndataR are optional Bioconductor integrations. No Python is required for canonical or NumPy I/O.

    The isolated installed candidate on this machine can be used with:

    AUDIT_ROOT=/Users/rh/Documents/GitHub/.repository-audits/cttir-public-20261030
export R_LIBS_USER="$AUDIT_ROOT/evidence/cellspecR/archive-library:$AUDIT_ROOT/tools/R-library"
Rscript --vanilla -e 'library(cellspecR); x <- cs_example(); p <- tempfile(); cs_write(x,p); stopifnot(all(cs_verify(p)$ok),identical(cs_cells(x),cs_cells(cs_read_cellspec(p)))); print(x)'
Rscript --vanilla -e 'shiny::runApp(cellspecR::cs_app(),host="127.0.0.1",port=18745)'

    For another machine, install the declared dependencies and run R CMD INSTALL on the prepared source archive. GitHub main does not yet contain these changes. The README provides the upload workflow and signal-policy example.

    Release gates and deferred work

    Local tests use synthetic fixtures. Comparative exports from actual supported QuPath/MCQuant/inForm versions remain a release-owner qualification task; no patient data were accessed. Run the hosted OS/R matrix on the accepted commit, select a final non-development version, refresh citation/deposit metadata and CRAN comments, rebuild/check the submission package, then obtain any necessary publication approval. No push, hosted candidate CI, CRAN submission or deposit has occurred.

    Readers hold NumPy arrays in memory and reject unsupported dimensions/integers; this is not a streaming solution for arbitrary-size archives. Canonical checksums establish consistency, not producer authentication, and canonical destination checks do not implement a concurrent-writer lock. Deployment beyond the default local Shiny session requires its own access-control and resource decisions.
